# Rebuttal Notes — Method Novelty (D1)

## ARR Policy Reference
- **H7**: "Do not penalize a method for being simple. If an approach is simple but well-motivated and effective, simplicity is a strength."

## Core Defense Points

### 1. Contribution is task formulation + empirical characterization, not feature engineering
- We introduce **ordinal depth estimation** as a new task (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+)
- No prior work addresses depth estimation in non-paraphrastic continuation chains
- The features are intentionally simple; the contribution is showing they exhibit differential depth response

### 2. Differential depth response is a novel empirical finding
- Three-gradient decomposition (drifting / moderate / stationary) has no prior documentation in inference-chain literature
- Lower-tail compression + upper-tail preservation pattern is new
- This is not a method paper — it is a measurement and characterization paper

### 3. Simplicity is a feature, not a bug
- 7-feature ensemble achieves binary F1=0.694 across 8 generators / 5 families
- Our approach: single lightweight reference model (Pythia-410M, 410M params)
- Their approach: four independent detection pipelines (each requiring separate inference)
- Interpretability: seven named statistics vs opaque ensemble

### 4. Scientific value independent of method complexity
- Establishes 3-class granularity ceiling (5-class fails, Appendix F)
- Documents prompt-type dependence bounds
- Negative downstream finding prevents wasted engineering effort
- Connection to model collapse literature (inference-chain drift as early indicator)

## Anticipated Objections and Responses

**"Just standard features"**: Features individually are standard; the contribution is (a) showing they decompose into depth-sensitive and depth-invariant groups, (b) that this decomposition generalizes across 8 generators / 5 families, (c) the ordinal task formulation.

**"Limited to base models"**: Deliberate design choice to isolate mechanism. Instruct results (F1 near chance) confirm this was the right call — instruction tuning confounds require separate study.

**"No deep learning method"**: QLoRA ceiling (F1=0.905) shows deep methods work better but don't change the scientific conclusions about DDR. Paper's value is the characterization, not maximizing F1.

\subsection{Comparison with Detection Baselines}
\label{sec:results-baselines}

We next ask whether existing detection methods---designed for binary real-vs-synthetic classification---incidentally capture depth structure, repurposing four detection scores as ordinal depth predictors under identical XGBoost and LOGO conditions (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}).
The strongest baseline is a 4-detector + surface feature ensemble (binary F1\,=\,0.708), which pools four detection scores with TTR and hapax ratio; among individual detectors, Avg-LogProb provides the most meaningful single-feature comparison.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\footnotesize
\caption{Depth classification (8-gen LOGO, pooled evaluation; pooled F1 is slightly higher than per-generator macro F1 in Table~\ref{tab:logo-results} because larger test folds from high-performing generators contribute proportionally more). Identical XGBoost configuration. 7-feature: one 410M model (905\,MB); 4-det ensembles: two models, 1.4B params (2{,}868\,MB). Individual detection scores (N/A) share the reference-model forward pass; per-method timing is not separately profiled. XGBoost uses 7 handcrafted scalar features (one 410M reference); QLoRA (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}) uses the full token sequence---an information-asymmetric ceiling, not a fair comparison.}
\label{tab:baselines}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Feat.} & \textbf{3-class F1} & \textbf{Bin F1} & \textbf{ms/text} \\
\midrule
4-det.\ + surface     & 6 & \textbf{0.795} & \textbf{0.708} & 22.8 \\
4-detector ens.\      & 4 & 0.785 & 0.700 & 22.8 \\
7-feature (ours)      & 7 & 0.774 & 0.705 & \textbf{9.7} \\
\midrule
Avg-LogProb           & 1 & 0.707 & 0.673 & --- \\
FastDetectGPT         & 1 & 0.660 & 0.569 & --- \\
LD-Score              & 1 & 0.630 & 0.675 & --- \\
Binoculars            & 1 & 0.411 & 0.539 & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

The 7-feature ensemble matches the 4-detector+surface ensemble on binary F1 (0.705 vs.\ 0.708; Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-ci}) at ${\sim}2.4\times$ lower cost, though the latter leads by 2.1\,pp on 3-class F1 (0.795 vs.\ 0.774); both surpass individual detectors by 3.0--16.6\,pp.
DDR's contribution is the decomposition into location-sensitive and shape-stable components (\S\ref{sec:discussion}), achieving comparable depth discrimination with a single 410M reference model; ordinal-specific methods (CORAL, Frank-Hall) yield comparable F1 (Appendix~\ref{app:classifier}).
Concurrent iterative-generation studies use different chain operators (back-translation, rephrasing) and target different phenomena (factuality, convergence dynamics), precluding direct inclusion as depth classification baselines (Appendix~\ref{app:iterative-comparison}).

-\looseness=-1 DDR reflects an empirical regularity of base-model autoregressive generation: recursive inputs compress the token-level NLL distribution monotonically (Appendix~\ref{app:nll-distribution}), shifting location features independently of the token-selection mechanism.
